facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s presented with a new pigmented lesion on his left second toenail
The lesion first appeared 12 months before presentation and was progressively growing
The lesion was asymptomatic
He was otherwise well and denied any fevers or weight loss
dark brown longitudinal pigment band covering the full length of the toenail of the left second digit with corresponding nail thickening over the pigmented band
The pigment was the same width throughout the band and extended to the proximal nail fold
No other nail or skin lesions were found at the time of examination
Bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix with invaginations of the epithelium
No melanocytic lesions observed
Immunostaining negative for S100 and CD34
Intracorneal hemorrhage and adjacent verrucous hyperkeratosis present
Villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate without melanocytic proliferation or keratinocyte atypia

concepts.why: The presence of bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix and villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate supports the diagnosis of onychopapilloma.
The dark brown longitudinal pigment band covering the full length of the toenail and extending to the proximal nail fold is consistent with longitudinal melanonychia.
The corresponding nail thickening over the pigmented band supports the diagnosis of onychauxis.
The presence of intracorneal hemorrhage and adjacent verrucous hyperkeratosis supports the diagnosis of verrucous hyperkeratosis.
The bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix is consistent with a nail matrix tumor.
The villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate support the diagnosis of a fibroepithelial tumor.
The presence of a dark brown longitudinal pigment band and corresponding nail thickening supports the diagnosis of nail dystrophy.
The presence of intracorneal hemorrhage and adjacent verrucous hyperkeratosis supports the diagnosis of subungual keratosis.
The absence of melanocytic lesions and negative immunostaining for S100 and CD34 explain the uncovered facts.
